I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live traffic feeds, so I can’t give you the real‑time traffic conditions for New York right now. However, if you’re looking for a quick snapshot of typical traffic patterns, here’s what you can expect:

| Time of Day | Typical Traffic Flow | Common Congested Areas |
|-------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| **Morning Rush (7 – 9 am)** | Heavy inbound traffic toward Midtown, Downtown, and the Financial District. | 5th Avenue, Broadway, West Side Highway, I‑87 (Adriatic Expressway). |
| **Midday (10 am – 2 pm)** | Moderate traffic; peaks around major intersections and near popular attractions. | Times Square, Bryant Park, 34th Street, 42nd Street. |
| **Afternoon (3 pm – 5 pm)** | Lightening of congestion as commuters head home. | 8th Avenue, 9th Avenue, East River Drive. |
| **Evening Rush (6 pm – 8 pm)** | Heavy outbound traffic from Midtown and Downtown. | 1st Avenue, 2nd Avenue, I‑95 (Brooklyn Bridge). |
| **Night (9 pm – midnight)** | Low traffic overall, but occasional congestion near nightlife hotspots. | 14th Street, 23rd Street, Lower East Side. |

If you need up‑to‑date traffic information, you could check a real‑time traffic service such as Google Maps, Waze, or the NYC Department of Transportation’s traffic cameras. Let me know if you’d like a quick guide on how to set up alerts or view live camera feeds!
